subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept `openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report` as the public delivery-report contract for self-delivered channel sends, or hold this under the broader outbound lifecycle hook parity design?
rationale: The code path is plausible, but naming, idempotency semantics, exported types, and generic-versus-channel-local ownership are public plugin SDK decisions that automation should not settle.

options.title: Accept the seam after proof
options.body: Require a rebase, redacted real WhatsApp/runtime proof, and focused maintainer signoff on the public API shape before merge.

options.title: Hold for the umbrella design
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and fold this API decision into the broader outbound lifecycle hook parity plan before accepting a new SDK subpath.

options.title: Channel-local only for now
options.body: Reject the public SDK surface for now and ask for a narrower WhatsApp-local implementation or a maintainer-authored core seam later.

recommendation.title: Accept the seam after proof
recommendation.body: Require a rebase, redacted real WhatsApp/runtime proof, and focused maintainer signoff on the public API shape before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans current core outbound, plugin SDK, and WhatsApp channel boundaries where the strongest current-main history signal points to steipete.
